nodes.statement:
If $X$ is an abelian variety, $Y$ a variety, and $f:Y\to X$ an etale
covering, then $Y$ has a unique abelian-variety structure for which $f$ is
a separable isogeny.
nodes.title: Serre--Lang

nodes.statement:
If $f:X\to Y$ is a proper smooth morphism of irreducible varieties with a
section, all fibres of $f$ are irreducible.
nodes.title: Irreducibility of fibres

nodes.statement:
If $f:Y\to X$ is an isogeny of abelian varieties, there is an isogeny
$g:X\to Y$ and $n>0$ with $g f=n_Y$ and $f g=n_X$: choose $n$ killing
$\ker f$, and factor multiplication by $n$ through the quotient by $\ker f$.
nodes.title: Quasi-inverse to an isogeny

nodes.statement:
For a pointed nonsingular variety, the pointed connected finite etale
coverings form an inverse system and
\[
\pi_1(X,x_0)=\varprojlim_{(Y,y_0,\pi)}G_Y.
\]
For an abelian variety $X$ with zero base point,
\[
\pi_1(X)\simeq\prod_lT_l(X),\qquad T_l(X)=\varprojlim_mX_{l^m}.
\]
For $l\ne p$, $T_l(X)\simeq\mathbb Z_l^{2g}$; if $r$ is the $p$-rank,
$T_p(X)=\varprojlim X^r_{p^m}\simeq\mathbb Z_p^r$.
nodes.title: Fundamental group and Tate modules

nodes.statement:
Put
$\operatorname{Hom}^0(X,Y)=\mathbb Q\otimes_\mathbb Z\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)$
and $\operatorname{End}^0X=\mathbb Q\otimes_\mathbb Z\operatorname{End}X$.
Composition makes abelian varieties up to isogeny a category, in which
isogenies are isomorphisms, and
\[
\operatorname{Hom}^0(X,Y)=\varinjlim_{X'\to X}\operatorname{Hom}(X',Y).
\]
nodes.title: Homomorphisms up to isogeny

nodes.statement:
If $Y$ is an abelian subvariety of $X$, there is an abelian subvariety $Z$
with $Y\cap Z$ finite and $Y+Z=X$; equivalently $X$ is isogenous to
$Y\times Z$.
nodes.title: Poincare complete reducibility

nodes.statement:
An abelian variety is simple if it has no abelian subvariety other than zero
and itself.
nodes.title: Simple abelian variety

nodes.statement:
Every abelian variety is isogenous to
$X_1^{n_1}\times\cdots\times X_k^{n_k}$ with the $X_i$ simple and pairwise
non-isogenous; the types and multiplicities are unique. If $X$ is simple,
$\operatorname{End}^0X$ is a division ring, and in general
\[
\operatorname{End}^0(X)=\bigoplus_iM_{n_i}(\operatorname{End}^0X_i).
\]
nodes.title: Simple decomposition

nodes.statement:
The function $\phi\mapsto\deg\phi$ on $\operatorname{End}X$ extends to a
homogeneous polynomial of degree $2g$ on $\operatorname{End}^0X$.
nodes.title: Degree polynomial

nodes.statement:
For abelian varieties $X,Y$, $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)$ is a finitely
generated free abelian group, and for $l\ne\operatorname{char}k$,
\[
\mathbb Z_l\otimes_\mathbb Z\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z_l}(T_l(X),T_l(Y))
\]
is injective. In characteristic zero over $\mathbb C$, restriction to the
lattices in $X_i=V_i/U_i$ injects Hom into
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(U_1,U_2)$.
nodes.title: Tate representation

nodes.statement:
$\operatorname{NS}(X)=\operatorname{Pic}X/\operatorname{Pic}^0X$ is free of
finite rank, and $\operatorname{End}X$ is a finite-dimensional semisimple
algebra over $\mathbb Q$.
nodes.title: Neron--Severi and endomorphism algebras

nodes.statement:
For a finite-dimensional associative simple separable algebra $A$ over
$\Gamma$, with center $\Lambda$, there are canonical reduced norm and trace
forms. Every norm is
$(\operatorname{Nm}_{\Lambda/\Gamma}\circ N^0)^k$ and every trace is
$\phi\circ\operatorname{Tr}^0$; if $[A:\Lambda]=d^2$, $N^0$ has degree $d$.
nodes.title: Norms and traces of simple algebras

nodes.statement:
For $f\in\operatorname{End}X$ and $l\ne\operatorname{char}k$,
\[
\deg f=\det T_l(f).
\]
Thus $\deg(n_X-f)=P(n)$, where $P(t)=\det(t-T_l(f))$ is monic of degree
$2g$ with integral rational coefficients and $P(f)=0$.
nodes.title: Degree and Tate determinant

nodes.statement:
The constant term and negative coefficient of $t^{2g-1}$ in the polynomial
above are respectively the norm and trace. If $X$ is simple, with center
$K$, $[K:\mathbb Q]=e$, and $[\operatorname{End}^0X:K]=d^2$, then $de\mid2g$.
It is of CM type precisely when $de=2g$, equivalently when
$\operatorname{End}^0X$ contains a field of degree $2g$ over $\mathbb Q$.
nodes.title: Characteristic and CM type

nodes.statement:
For $l\ne\operatorname{char}k$, put
$M_l=\varprojlim\mu_{l^n}\simeq\mathbb Z_l$. For $n$ prime to the
characteristic, the kernels of $n_X$ and $n_{\widehat X}$ have a canonical
pairing $\bar e_n:X_n\times(\widehat X)_n\to\mu_n$.
nodes.title: Tate pairing

nodes.statement:
If $(f)=nD$ and $(g)=n_X^{-1}(D)$, then
\[
\bar e_n(a,\lambda)=g(x)/g(x+a).
\]
nodes.title: Divisor formula for the pairing

nodes.statement:
For coprime $m,n$, $x\in X_{mn}$ and $y\in(\widehat X)_{mn}$,
\[
\bar e_n(mx,my)=\bar e_{mn}(x,y)^m.
\]
nodes.title: Compatibility of pairings

nodes.statement:
There is a natural non-degenerate $\mathbb Z_l$-bilinear pairing
\[
e_l:T_l(X)\times T_l(\widehat X)\longrightarrow M_l.
\]
If $f:X\to Y$ has dual $\widehat f$, then
\[
e_l(T_l(f)\xi,\eta)=e_l(\xi,T_l(\widehat f)\eta).
\]
For a line bundle $L$ on $X$, define
\[
E^L(x,y)=e_l(x,T_l(\phi_L)(y)).
\]
nodes.title: Tate pairing and Riemann form

nodes.statement:
The form $E^L$ is skew-symmetric for every line bundle $L$.
Consequently $L\mapsto E^L$ injects
\[
\operatorname{NS}(X)\longrightarrow
\{\text{alternating forms }T_l(X)\times T_l(X)\to M_l\}.
\]
nodes.title: Skew-symmetry of the Riemann form

nodes.statement:
For a homomorphism $f:X\to Y$ and a line bundle $L$ on $Y$,
\[
E^{f^*L}(x,y)=E^L(T_l(f)x,T_l(f)y).
\]
nodes.title: Pullback of Riemann forms

nodes.statement:
Under $T_l(X\times\widehat X)=T_l(X)\times T_l(\widehat X)$,
\[
E^P((x,\widehat x),(y,\widehat y))
=e_l(x,\widehat y)-e_l(y,\widehat x).
\]
nodes.title: The Poincare Riemann form

nodes.statement:
For a homomorphism $\phi:X\to\widehat X$, the form
$e_l(x,\phi(y))$ is skew-symmetric if and only if there is a line bundle
$L$ with $2\phi=\phi_L$.
nodes.title: Skew forms and line bundles

nodes.statement:
For ample $L$ on $X$, define
\[
\phi'=\phi_L^{-1}\widehat\phi\phi_L.
\]
Then $'$ is a $\mathbb Q$-linear involution,
$(\phi\psi)'=\psi'\phi'$, and
\[
E^L(\phi x,y)=E^L(x,\phi'y).
\]
nodes.title: Rosati involution

nodes.statement:
Under $\operatorname{Hom}^0(X,\widehat X)\simeq\operatorname{End}^0X$ via
$\psi\mapsto\phi_L^{-1}\psi$, the space
$\mathbb Q\otimes\operatorname{NS}(X)$ is exactly the fixed subspace of
the Rosati involution.
nodes.title: Neron--Severi classes and Rosati fixed points

nodes.statement:
There is a generator
$v\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z_l}(\Lambda^2T_l(X),M_l)$ such that
for divisors $D_i$ and $E_i=E^{\mathcal O_X(D_i)}$,
\[
E_1\wedge\cdots\wedge E_g=(D_1\cdots D_g)v.
\]
nodes.title: Wedge and intersection numbers

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is simple and $K\subset\operatorname{End}^0X$ is a $\mathbb Q$-subalgebra
fixed by Rosati, then $[K:\mathbb Q]$ divides $\dim X$.
nodes.title: Degree of a fixed subalgebra

nodes.statement:
For an ample divisor $H$, $L=\mathcal O_X(H)$, and the Rosati involution
defined by $L$,
\[
\operatorname{Tr}(\phi\phi')
=\frac{2g}{(H^g)}(H^{g-1}\cdot\phi^*H),
\]
and $\phi\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(\phi\phi')$ is positive definite.
nodes.title: Positive Rosati trace

nodes.statement:
For simple $X$, $D=\operatorname{End}^0X$ is a division algebra with a
positive involution. If $K$ is its center, $K_0=\{x\in K:x'=x\}$,
$[D:K]=d^2$, and $[K:\mathbb Q]=e$, then $K_0$ is totally real. If
$K\ne K_0$, it is totally imaginary over $K_0$ and the involution is of the
second kind; otherwise it is of the first kind. In the nontrivial Brauer
class case of the first kind, $D$ is a quaternion division algebra.
nodes.title: Simple endomorphism algebras: initial classification

nodes.statement:
For a division algebra $D$ with positive involution, the involution is one of
the Albert types: (I) a totally real field with identity involution; (II)
a quaternion division algebra over a totally real field with an orthogonal
involution; (III) a quaternion division algebra with its canonical
involution; or (IV) an algebra with totally imaginary quadratic center over
a totally real fixed field, with conjugation on the complex factors.
nodes.title: Brauer groups and positive involutions

nodes.statement:
For $S=\{x\in D:x'=x\}$, $\eta=\dim_{\mathbb Q}S/\dim_{\mathbb Q}D$,
and $[D:K]=d^2$, $[K_0:\mathbb Q]=e_0$, the four types have
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{type}&e&d&\eta\\ \hline
I&e_0&1&1\\ II&e_0&2&1/2\\ III&e_0&2&1/2\\ IV&2e_0&d&1/2.
\end{array}
\]
For endomorphism algebras of simple abelian varieties these invariants obey
the divisibility restrictions by $g=\dim X$.
nodes.title: Albert numerical table

nodes.statement:
If $\alpha'\alpha=a\in\mathbb Z$ and $\omega_i$ are the roots of the
characteristic polynomial of $\alpha$, then $\mathbb Q[\alpha]$ is
semisimple, $|\omega_i|^2=a$, and $\omega_i\mapsto a/\omega_i$ permutes
the roots.
nodes.title: Characteristic roots

nodes.statement:
If $X_0$ is a scheme over $\mathbb F_q$ whose base change $X$ is an abelian
variety, then $X_0(\mathbb F_q)\ne\varnothing$. If $\pi$ is Frobenius and
$\omega_i$ are its characteristic roots, then
\[
\#X(\mathbb F_{q^n})=\prod_i(1-\omega_i^n),
\qquad |\omega_i|=\sqrt q,
\qquad \omega_{\pi(i)}=q/\omega_i.
\]
nodes.title: Lang and Weil

nodes.statement:
For some constant $C$,
$|\#X(\mathbb F_{q^n})-q^{ng}|\le Cq^{n(g-1/2)}$.
nodes.title: Weil estimate

nodes.statement:
For $n\ge3$ and ample $L$, the restriction from automorphisms preserving
$L$ modulo $\operatorname{Pic}^0X$ to $\operatorname{Aut}(X_n)$ is injective.
nodes.title: Serre torsion restriction

nodes.statement:
For an ample $L$,
\[
NS^0(X)\simeq\{\alpha\in\operatorname{End}^0X:\alpha'=\alpha\}.
\]
With product $\alpha\circ\beta=(\alpha\beta+\beta\alpha)/2$, this is a
formally real Jordan algebra, a product over $\mathbb R$ of real symmetric,
complex Hermitian, and quaternionic Hermitian matrix algebras. Ample bundles
are exactly its totally positive elements.
nodes.title: Real structure of $NS^0$

nodes.statement:
Let $K_0$ be totally real of degree $g$ and $K$ a totally imaginary quadratic
extension. The pairs $(X,i)$ with $X/\mathbb C$ an abelian variety and
$i:K\hookrightarrow\operatorname{End}^0X$ have exactly $2^g$ isomorphism
classes up to isogeny. Representatives are
$X(K,\Phi)=(\mathbb R\otimes_{\mathbb Q}K)/A_0$, one for each of the
$2^g$ complex-algebra structures $\Phi$ on $\mathbb R\otimes K$.
nodes.title: CM complex-torus classification

nodes.statement:
For an elliptic curve in characteristic $p$, non-finite-field definition is
equivalent to $\operatorname{End}^0X=\mathbb Q$. If $X$ is defined over a
finite field, its endomorphism algebra is imaginary quadratic exactly when
the $p$-rank is one; for $p$-rank zero it is the quaternion division algebra
with local invariants $\operatorname{Inv}_p=\operatorname{Inv}_\infty=1/2$
and all other finite invariants zero.
nodes.title: Deuring

nodes.statement:
A simple abelian variety in characteristic $p$ is isogenous to one defined
over a finite field if and only if it is of CM type.
nodes.title: CM over finite fields

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is defined over a finite field $k_0$, with Frobenius $\pi$, then
\[
\operatorname{End}(X,k_0)\otimes\mathbb Q_l
=\operatorname{Cent}_{\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q_l}(T_lX)}(T_l\pi).
\]
nodes.title: Tate centralizer theorem

nodes.statement:
A theta-group is an exact sequence
\[
1\to\mathbb G_m\xrightarrow{i}G\xrightarrow{\pi}K\to1
\]
where $K$ is commutative, the sequence is locally split, $i$ is a closed
immersion identifying the kernel, and $\mathbb G_m$ is central. For finite
$K$, a section identifies the underlying scheme with
$\mathbb G_m\times K$ and the group law with
\[
(\alpha,k)(\alpha',k')=(\alpha\alpha'f(k,k'),k+k'),
\]
where $f$ is a 2-cocycle, defined up to coboundary.
nodes.title: Theta group

nodes.statement:
The commutator defines a skew-symmetric bihomomorphism
$e:K\times K\to\mathbb G_m$, and hence a homomorphism
$\gamma:K\to\widehat K$ with
$e(k,k')=\langle k,\gamma(k')\rangle$. The center of $G$ maps to
$\ker\gamma$; if $K$ is finite, the center is exactly $\mathbb G_m$ iff
$\gamma$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.title: Theta commutator

nodes.statement:
If $K$ is finite and $G$ commutative, then
$G\simeq\mathbb G_m\times K$ as a group. If $K$ has prime order, then $G$
is commutative.
nodes.title: Trivial theta extensions

nodes.statement:
For a line bundle $L$ on an abelian variety $X$, the functor of automorphisms
of $S\times L$ covering translations of $S\times X$ is represented by a
group scheme $\mathcal G(L)$, fitting into a theta-group extension
\[
1\to\mathbb G_m\to\mathcal G(L)\to K(L)\to1.
\]
nodes.title: Theta group of a line bundle

nodes.statement:
The theta group $\mathcal G(L)$ has a skew-symmetric bihomomorphism
\[
e^L:K(L)\times K(L)\to\mathbb G_m
\]
defined by its commutator. If $L\in\operatorname{Pic}^0X$, then $K(L)=X$,
so $e^L=1$ and $\mathcal G(L)$ is commutative.
nodes.title: Commutator pairing of a line bundle
Functoriality of commutator pairings

nodes.statement:
For an isogeny $\pi:X\to Y$ and a line bundle $L$ on $X$, line bundles $M$
on $Y$ with $\pi^*M\simeq L$ correspond naturally to homomorphisms
$\alpha:\ker\pi\to\mathcal G(L)$ lifting the inclusion into $X$.
Such an $M$ exists iff $\ker\pi\subset K(L)$ and
$e^L$ is trivial on $\ker\pi\times\ker\pi$.
nodes.title: Descent of line bundles

nodes.statement:
For a line bundle $L$ and integer $n$, $L\simeq M^n$ for some $M$ iff
$K(L)\supset X_n$.
nodes.title: Power criterion

nodes.statement:
For a skew bihomomorphism $e:K\times K\to\mathbb G_m$ and subgroup $H$,
$H^\perp$ is the kernel of $K\xrightarrow\gamma\widehat K\to\widehat H$;
equivalently it consists of points pairing trivially with every base change of
every point of $H$. If $L=\pi^*M$ and $H=\ker\pi$, then
$K(M)\simeq H^\perp/H$.
nodes.title: Orthogonal subgroup

nodes.statement:
If $L$ is non-degenerate and $H\subset K(L)$ is maximal with
$e^L|_{H\times H}=1$, then $H=H^\perp$ and
\[
\operatorname{order}(H)^2=\operatorname{order}(K(L)).
\]
nodes.title: Maximal isotropic subgroup

nodes.statement:
Every abelian variety is isogenous to a principally polarized one. If $L$ is
non-degenerate, then $\mathcal G(L)$ is a non-degenerate theta group.
nodes.title: Principal polarization and non-degeneracy

nodes.statement:
Let $L=L(H,\alpha)$ be a line bundle on $X=V/U$, let $E={\rm Im}\,H$, and
let $\pi:V\to X$ be the natural map. For $u,v\in U^\perp$,
\[
 e^{-2\pi iE(u,v)}=e^L(\pi u,\pi v).
\]
nodes.title: Analytic theta-group comparison

nodes.statement:
For $X=V/U$ and $\ell$, the canonical pairing $E^L$ on $T_\ell X$ is, up to
sign, the $\mathbb Z_\ell$-linear extension of $E:U\times U\to\mathbb Z$.
In particular, for the Poincare bundle on $Y\times\widehat Y$, the analytic
pairing of $U,\widehat U$ agrees up to sign with the canonical pairing of
$T_\ell Y,T_\ell\widehat Y$.
nodes.title: Analytic and l-adic Riemann pairings

nodes.statement:
Analytically,
\[
{\rm End}^0(X)=\{T:V\to V\text{ complex-linear}:T(\mathbb Q\cdot U)\subset\mathbb Q\cdot U\},
\]
and the Rosati involution is the $H$-adjoint $T^*$ defined by
$H(T^*x,y)=H(x,Ty)$. It equals the algebraic Rosati involution and satisfies
\[
{\rm Tr}(T^*T)\ge0,\qquad T\ne0.
\]
nodes.title: Analytic interpretation and positivity of Rosati

nodes.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of varieties with $X$ an abelian variety. If
$F_x$ is the connected component of the fibre $f^{-1}(f(x))$ containing $x$,
then there is a closed connected subgroup $F\subset X$ such that
$F_x=x+F$ for every $x$.
nodes.title: Fibres of a morphism from an abelian variety

nodes.statement:
For an effective divisor $D$ on an abelian variety $X$, let
$H(D)=\{x\mid T_x^*D=D\}$ (equality of divisors), let $L=L(D)$, and let
$f:X\to\mathbf P(H^0(X,L^2))$ be the morphism defined by the base-point-free
bundle $L^2$. If $F(D)=\ker f$, then
\[
H(D)\text{ is Zariski closed},\qquad H(D)^0=K(L)^0=F(D).
\]

\emph{The source states this theorem without proof.}
nodes.title: Effective divisors and their stabilizers
Maximal triviality subscheme

nodes.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be complete varieties, $Z$ a connected scheme, and $L$ a line
bundle on $X\times Y\times Z$. If the restrictions to
\(\{x_0\}\times Y\times Z$, $X\times\{y_0\}\times Z$ and
$X\times Y\times\{z_0\}$ are trivial, then $L$ is trivial.
nodes.title: Theorem of the cube, scheme-theoretic form

nodes.statement:
A group scheme is a scheme $G$ with morphisms $m:G\times G\to G$,
$e:\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$, and $i:G\to G$ satisfying associativity,
identity, and inverse diagrams. Equivalently, $G(S)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(S,G)$
is a group, functorially in $S$. The functor $X\mapsto\underline X$ is fully
faithful (Yoneda).
nodes.title: Group scheme and functor of points

nodes.statement:
For a group scheme $G$, every tangent vector at $e$ extends uniquely to a
left-invariant vector field. The left-invariant vector fields form the Lie
algebra of $G$ under the Poisson bracket, and in characteristic $p$ under
the $p$-th power operation.
nodes.title: Lie algebra of a group scheme

nodes.statement:
The bracket is bilinear, alternating, and satisfies Jacobi. In characteristic
$p$, $\operatorname{ad}(X^p)=(\operatorname{ad}X)^p$ and
\[
(X+Y)^p=X^p+Y^p+F_p(\operatorname{ad}X,\operatorname{ad}Y)Y.
\]
If $G$ is commutative, the bracket is zero: using
$k[\epsilon,\epsilon']/ (\epsilon^2,\epsilon'^2)$, the commutator of the
two infinitesimal translations is the translation by the commutator of two
$S$-valued points, which is the identity.
nodes.title: Lie identities and commutative groups

nodes.statement: Every group scheme over a field of characteristic zero is smooth and reduced.
nodes.title: Characteristic-zero smoothness

nodes.statement:
A closed subscheme $H\subset G$ is a subgroup scheme if multiplication on
$H\times H$ factors through $H$. The fibre over the identity of a homomorphism
of group schemes is its kernel and is a closed subgroup scheme.
In characteristic $p$, with $\mathfrak m$ the maximal ideal at $e$, the
subscheme $G_n=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_e/\mathfrak m^{(p^n)})$ is a
subgroup scheme and $\Lie(G_n)=\Lie(G)$ for $n\ge1$.
nodes.title: Subgroup schemes and kernels

nodes.statement:
Put
\[
H_x=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(\mathcal O_{x,G},k),\qquad
H=\bigoplus_{x\in G}H_x
 =\varinjlim_{Z\subset G\ {\text{finite}}}\Gamma(\mathcal O_Z)^*.
\]
The convolution is
\[
L_1*L_2(f)=L_1\otimes L_2(m^*f).
\]
The elements $\delta_x$ are convolution identities at points,
$\delta_e*L=L*\delta_e=L$, and evaluation at $1$ is the augmentation.
nodes.title: Hyperalgebra

nodes.statement:
Each $L\in H$ defines a left-invariant differential operator
\[
D_L(f)=(L\otimes1)m^*(f),\qquad D_Lf(e)=L(f),
\]
and $D_{L_1*L_2}=D_{L_1}\circ D_{L_2}$. If $G$ is commutative, $H$ is
commutative and the Lie bracket is zero.
nodes.title: Invariant differential operators

nodes.statement:
An action is a morphism $\mu:G\times X\to X$ satisfying the unit and
associativity diagrams. A morphism is invariant if $f\mu=fp_2$. The action
is free if $(\mu,p_2):G\times X\to X\times X$ is a closed immersion.
A $G$-linearization of a coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism
$p_2^*\mathcal F\simeq\mu^*\mathcal F$ satisfying the corresponding
associativity diagram and restricting to the identity at $e$.
nodes.title: Action and freeness

nodes.statement:
Let a finite group scheme $G$ act on $X$, with every orbit contained in an
affine open. There is a quotient $(Y,\pi)$ whose underlying topological
space is the orbit quotient and for which
$\mathcal O_Y\simeq\pi_*\mathcal O_X^G$. It is unique, finite and
surjective, and has the universal property for invariant morphisms.
If the action is free, $\pi$ is flat of degree $n=\dim_kR$ for
$G=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $G\times X\simeq X\times_YX$, and pullback is an
equivalence between coherent sheaves on $Y$ and coherent $G$-sheaves on $X$.
nodes.title: Quotient by a finite group scheme

nodes.statement:
A homomorphism $f:X\to Y$ is an epimorphism if it is surjective and
$f^*:\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ is injective.
nodes.title: Epimorphism of group schemes

nodes.statement:
If a finite normal subgroup scheme $G\subset X$ acts by right translations,
then $X/G$ is a group scheme, $\pi:X\to X/G$ is an epimorphism, and
$G=\ker(\pi)$. Conversely, an epimorphism with finite kernel is the quotient
by its kernel.
nodes.title: Finite normal quotients

nodes.statement:
If $Y=X/G$ and $\mathcal G$ is a coherent $G$-sheaf on $X$, then
\[
\pi^*(\pi_*\mathcal G)\simeq\mathcal G\otimes_kR,
\qquad G=\operatorname{Spec}R.
\]
nodes.title: Base change for equivariant sheaves

nodes.statement:
Let a finite group scheme $G$ act freely on $X$, with quotient $X/G$, and
let $F$ be a finite scheme with a $G$-action. The induced free action on
$X\times F$ has quotient
\[
U=(X\times F)/G,
\]
and the natural morphism $\pi:U\to V=X/G$ is called the fibration with
fibre $F$ associated to the principal $G$-bundle $X\to X/G$. It is finite
and flat; its degree is the rank of $\pi_*\mathcal O_U$ over
$\mathcal O_V$.
nodes.title: Fibration with finite fibre

nodes.statement:
If $\pi:U\to V$ is a finite-fibre fibration associated to a principal
$G$-bundle, then for every coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $V$,
\[
\chi(\pi^*\mathcal F)=(\deg\pi)\chi(\mathcal F).
\]
nodes.title: Euler characteristic of an associated fibration

nodes.statement:
Every finite étale morphism $f:U\to V$ of constant degree $n$ is an
associated finite-fibre fibration for a principal $\Sigma(n)$-space. In the
$n$-fold fibre product $U\times_V\cdots\times_VU$, let $P$ be the open and
closed locus of tuples with pairwise distinct entries. Then $P\to V$ is a
principal $\Sigma(n)$-space. If $F$ is the reduced $n$-point scheme with
the natural permutation action, the invariant map
\[
P\times F\longrightarrow V,
\qquad ((x_1,\ldots,x_n),i)\longmapsto x_i
\]
has quotient $V$ and identifies the associated space with $U$.
nodes.title: Finite étale maps as associated spaces

nodes.statement:
For a line bundle $L$ on an abelian variety $X$, put
\[
M=m^*L\otimes p_1^*L^{-1}\otimes p_2^*L^{-1}
\]
on $X\times X$. The group scheme $K(L)\subset X$ is the maximal closed
subscheme for which $M|_{K(L)\times X}$ is trivial. Equivalently, for every
scheme $S$ and $f:S\to X$, one has $f\in K(L)(S)$ exactly when
\[
T_f^*L_S\simeq L_S\otimes p_2^*N
\]
for a line bundle $N$ on $S$.
nodes.title: Scheme-theoretic stabilizer of a line bundle

nodes.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $L$ a line bundle on $S\times X$, trivial on
$S\times\{0\}$, whose restriction to every fibre $\{s\}\times X$ lies in
$\operatorname{Pic}^0X$. There is a unique morphism $\phi:S\to\widehat X$
such that $L\simeq(\phi\times1_X)^*P$.
nodes.title: Universal Poincare mapping property

nodes.statement:
For an abelian variety $X$ of dimension $g$ and its dual $\widehat X$,
\[
H^i(\widehat X\times X,P)=
\begin{cases}0&i\ne g,\\ k&i=g.\end{cases}
\]
nodes.title: Cohomology of the Poincare bundle

nodes.statement:
For $\dim X=g$,
\[
\dim_kH^p(X,\mathcal O_X)=\binom gp.
\]
nodes.title: Structure-sheaf cohomology

nodes.statement:
There is a canonical isomorphism
$T_0\widehat X\simeq H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$.
nodes.title: Tangent space of the dual

nodes.statement:
If $f:X\to Y$ is an isogeny, there is a unique homomorphism
$\widehat f:\widehat Y\to\widehat X$ with
\[
(1\times\widehat f)^*P_X\simeq(f\times1)^*P_Y,
\]
and $\deg f=\deg\widehat f$.
nodes.title: Dual isogenies

nodes.statement:
For every line bundle $L$ on $X$, $\phi_L:X\to\operatorname{Pic}^0X\simeq
\widehat X$ is a morphism and its scheme-theoretic kernel is $K(L)$.
nodes.title: The morphism associated to a line bundle
Divisorial correspondences

nodes.statement:
The canonical morphism $X\to\widehat{\widehat X}$ defined by the Poincare
bundle is an isomorphism.
nodes.title: Duality hypothesis

nodes.statement:
For a finite commutative group scheme $G=\operatorname{Spec}R$ in
characteristic $p>0$, the dual group scheme is
$\widehat G=\operatorname{Spec}R^*$, where the dual of the group-law
coproduct is the multiplication on $R^*$ and the dual of multiplication on
$R$ is its coproduct.
nodes.title: Cartier dual

nodes.statement:
For every scheme $S$,
\[
\widehat G(S)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_S(G_S,\mathbb G_{m,S}),
\]
functorially in $S$.
nodes.title: Cartier dual represents characters

nodes.statement:
Every finite commutative group scheme has a unique product decomposition
$G_{r,r}\times G_{r,l}\times G_{l,r}\times G_{l,l}$ according as it and
its Cartier dual are reduced or local. Groups of type $(r,r)$ are products
of cyclic groups of order prime to $p$; groups of type $(r,l)$ are products
of cyclic $p$-groups and type $(l,r)$ are their duals.
nodes.title: Local/reduced decomposition

nodes.statement:
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Gp.Sch}}(\widehat G,\mathbb G_a)
\simeq\{\alpha\in R^*:s^*\alpha=\alpha\otimes1+1\otimes\alpha\}
\simeq\Lie(G).
\]
The $p$-power operation corresponds to composition with Frobenius.
nodes.title: Primitive elements and the Lie algebra

nodes.statement:
A finite group scheme is of height one if it has one point $e$ and
$x^p=0$ for every $x$ in the maximal ideal at $e$.
nodes.title: Height one

nodes.statement:
The functor $G\mapsto\Lie G$ is an equivalence between finite commutative
height-one group schemes and finite-dimensional $p$-Lie algebras.
nodes.title: Height-one group schemes and $p$-Lie algebras

nodes.statement:
For a commutative height-one $G$ with Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, an action on
$X$ is equivalent to derivations $D_\alpha$ satisfying
\[
[D_\alpha,D_\beta]=0,\qquad D_{\alpha^{(p)}}=D_\alpha^p.
\]
Moreover multiplication by $p$ on $G$ is zero.
nodes.title: Actions of height-one groups

nodes.statement:
Any vector space with a $p$-linear operation decomposes uniquely as
$V=V_s\oplus V_n$, with a basis of fixed vectors on $V_s$ and nilpotent
$p$-operation on $V_n$. For a height-one group this is the decomposition
$\Lie G_{l,r}\oplus\Lie G_{l,l}$.
nodes.title: Semisimple/nilpotent decomposition

nodes.statement:
If $f:X\to Y$ is an isogeny with kernel $K$ and dual map
$\widehat f:\widehat Y\to\widehat X$ with kernel $K'$, then
$K'\simeq\widehat K$ canonically.
nodes.title: Kernel of the dual isogeny

nodes.statement:
An isogeny $f:X\to Y$ is of height one if $k(X)^p\subset k(Y)$.
This is equivalent to its kernel being a height-one group scheme.
nodes.title: Height-one isogeny

nodes.statement:
Height-one isogenies out of $X$, up to isomorphism, correspond one-to-one to
$p$-Lie subalgebras of $\Lie X$.
nodes.title: Height-one isogenies and $p$-Lie subalgebras

nodes.statement:
Under $\Lie\widehat X\simeq H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, the $p$-power operation
on $\Lie\widehat X$ is the Frobenius map on $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$.
nodes.title: Frobenius and the Hasse--Witt operation

nodes.statement:
For $L\simeq\mathcal O_X(D)$ on a $g$-dimensional abelian variety,
\[
\chi(L)=\frac{(D^g)}{g!},\qquad \chi(L)^2=\deg\phi_L.
\]
nodes.title: Riemann--Roch

nodes.statement:
Over $\mathbf C$, for $L=L(H,\alpha)$ with $K(L)$ finite,
\[
 \deg\phi_L=\operatorname{order}K(L)
 =\operatorname{order}(U^\perp/U)=\det(E(u_i,u_j)),
 \qquad |\chi(L)|=\sqrt{\det(E(u_i,u_j))}.
\]
Thus $|\chi(L)|$ is the Pfaffian of the skew matrix $(E(u_i,u_j))$ up to
sign, since $\operatorname{pf}(A)^2=\det A$.
nodes.title: Analytic degree and Pfaffian

nodes.statement:
If $K(L)$ is finite, there is a unique $i(L)$ with
$H^p(X,L)=0$ for $p\ne i(L)$ and $H^{i(L)}(X,L)\ne0$, and
$i(L^{-1})=g-i(L)$.
nodes.title: Vanishing and index

nodes.statement:
For a projective $r$-fold and line bundles $L_1,\ldots,L_k$, there is $c$
such that
\[
\dim H^i(L_1^{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes L_k^{a_k})
<c(1+|a|^r).
\]
nodes.title: Polynomial growth of cohomology

nodes.statement:
If $L$ is ample and $M$ non-degenerate on a $g$-fold, the polynomial
$P(t)=\chi(L^t\otimes M)$ has all roots real, and $i(M)$ is the number of
positive roots counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Index polynomial

nodes.statement:
For $P(n,m)=\chi(L^n\otimes M^m)$, choose $q>0$ and integers $r_i$ with
$q^{-1}(r_i-1)<t_i<q^{-1}r_i$, where $t_i$ are the real roots of
$P(t,1)$. By the preceding index comparisons,
\[
i(r_k)\le i(r_k-1)=i(r_{k-1})\le\cdots\le i(r_1-1)=i(0),
\]
and $i(r_i-1)-i(r_i)\le\lambda_i$. For large positive $r$, $i(r)=0$,
and for large negative $r$, $i(r)=g$. Hence
\[
g=i(\text{very negative }r)-i(\text{very positive }r)\le\sum_i\lambda_i.
\]
Since $P$ has degree at most $g$, equality holds; $i(0)=i(M)$ is the sum
of multiplicities of positive roots.
nodes.title: Completion of the index root count

nodes.statement:
If $X=V/U$ and $L=L(H,\alpha)$ is non-degenerate, then $i(L)$ is the
number of negative eigenvalues of $H$. Choosing an ample
$L_0=L(H_0,\alpha_0)$,
\[
\chi(L_0^n\otimes L)=\operatorname{pf}(nE_0+E),
\qquad E=\operatorname{Im}H.
\]
Diagonalizing relative to $H_0$, $H(e_i,e_j)=\lambda_i\delta_{ij}$, the
Pfaffian is $\prod_i(n+\lambda_i)$, proving the assertion.
nodes.title: Complex index and eigenvalues

nodes.statement:
For any ample line bundle $L$ on an abelian variety $X$, $L^n$ is very ample
if $n>3$.
nodes.title: Very ampleness of powers

nodes.statement:
An abelian variety $X$ is a complete algebraic variety over an algebraically
closed field $k$ with a group law $m:X\times X\to X$ such that $m$ and the
inverse map are morphisms of varieties.
nodes.title: Abelian variety

nodes.statement:
If $g=\dim X$, then
\[
 X_n\simeq(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g}\quad(\operatorname{char}k\nmid n),
 \qquad X_{p^m}\simeq(\mathbf Z/p^m\mathbf Z)^i
\]
for $p=\operatorname{char}k$, where $0\le i\le g$; $X$ is commutative and
divisible. Moreover
\[
 H^q(X,\Omega^p)\simeq\bigwedge^p H^1(X,\Omega^1)\otimes_k
 \bigwedge^q H^1(X,\mathcal O_X),
\quad \dim H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)=\dim H^0(X,\Omega^1)=g.
\]
nodes.title: Basic structure
Translations

nodes.statement:
If $g=\dim X$ and $p=\operatorname{char}k$, then the algebraic fundamental group
has the expected form
\[
 \pi_1(X)\simeq\prod_\ell(\mathbf Z_\ell)^{2g}\quad(p=0),\qquad
 \pi_1(X)\simeq\prod_{\ell\ne p}(\mathbf Z_\ell)^{2g}\times\mathbf Z_p^i
 \quad(p>0),
\]
where $i$ is the $p$-rank.  More generally, if a finite group acts freely on a
variety $Y$ with quotient $X$, then some $n>0$ and homomorphisms fit into
\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}&&Y&&\\[-2pt]&\swarrow&&\searrow&\\[-2pt]
X&&\xrightarrow{\,n_X\,}&&X.
\end{array}
\]
The variety $Y$ carries an abelian-variety structure for which both maps are
homomorphisms.
nodes.title: Fundamental group and free finite quotients

nodes.statement: An abelian variety is everywhere nonsingular.
nodes.title: Everywhere nonsingular

nodes.statement: An abelian variety is commutative.
nodes.title: First commutativity proof

nodes.statement:
If $T=T_{X,0}$ and $\Omega_0=T^*_{X,0}$, then
\[
 \Omega_0\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_X^1.
\]
Every regular differential form on $X$ is translation invariant.
nodes.title: Invariant differentials

nodes.statement: For every $n$ not divisible by $\operatorname{char}k$, $n_X$ is surjective.
nodes.title: Prime-to-characteristic multiplication

nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be complete, $Y,Z$ varieties, and $f:X\times Y\to Z$ a morphism such
that $f(X\times\{y_0\})=\{z_0\}$. Then $f=g\circ p_2$ for a morphism
$g:Y\to Z$.
nodes.title: Rigidity Lemma, Form I

nodes.statement:
If $X,Y$ are abelian varieties and $f:X\to Y$ is a morphism, then
$f(x)=h(x)+a$ for a homomorphism $h$ and $a\in Y$.
nodes.title: Morphisms are homomorphisms up to translation

nodes.statement: An abelian variety is commutative.
nodes.title: Second commutativity proof

nodes.statement:
For pointed complete varieties $S,T$ and an abelian variety $X$,
\[
 \Hom(S,X)\times\Hom(T,X)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Hom(S\times T,X),
 \qquad(f,g)\mapsto[(s,t)\mapsto f(s)+g(t)].
\]
nodes.title: Linearity of maps into an abelian variety

nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be complete, $e\in X$, and $m:X\times X\to X$ satisfy
$m(x,e)=m(e,x)=x$. Then $m$ is an abelian-variety group law with identity $e$.
nodes.title: Recognition criterion

nodes.statement:
If $f:X\to Y$ is proper between locally noetherian preschemes and $\mathcal F$
is coherent, then $R^pf_*\mathcal F$ is coherent for all $p\ge0$.
nodes.title: Coherence of proper direct images

nodes.statement:
A quasicoherent $\mathcal F$ on $X$ is $f$-flat if every $\mathcal F_x$ is
$\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}$-flat; equivalently, sections over affine $U$ mapping into
affine $V$ are flat $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-modules.
nodes.title: Flat over the base

nodes.statement:
For proper $f:X\to Y$ with $Y=\Spec A$, $X$ noetherian, and coherent
$\mathcal F$ flat over $Y$, there is a finite complex $K^\bullet$ of finitely generated
projective $A$-modules such that, functorially for every $A$-algebra $B$,
\[
 H^p(X\times_Y\Spec B,\mathcal F\otimes_A B)
 \simeq H^p(K^\bullet\otimes_A B).
\]
nodes.title: Cohomology and base change complex

nodes.statement:
Let $C^\bullet$ be bounded over a noetherian ring $A$, with finitely generated
cohomology. There is a bounded complex $K^\bullet$ of finite modules, free in
positive degrees, mapping quasi-isomorphically to $C^\bullet$; if $C^p$ are
flat, $K^0$ is flat.
nodes.title: Finite complex model

nodes.statement:
If finite complexes of flat $A$-modules are quasi-isomorphic, then their
cohomologies remain isomorphic after tensoring with every $A$-algebra $B$.
nodes.title: Flat complexes commute with arbitrary base change

nodes.statement:
For proper $f:X\to Y$ and coherent $\mathcal F$ flat over $Y$, the function
$y\mapsto\dim_{k(y)}H^p(X_y,\mathcal F_y)$ is upper semicontinuous, while
$y\mapsto\chi(\mathcal F_y)$ is locally constant.
nodes.title: Semicontinuity and Euler characteristic

nodes.statement:
If $Y$ is reduced and connected, constancy of
$y\mapsto\dim H^p(X_y,\mathcal F_y)$ is equivalent to $R^pf_*\mathcal F$
being locally free and having fibers $H^p(X_y,\mathcal F_y)$. Under these
conditions the same base-change map is an isomorphism in degree $p-1$.
nodes.title: Base-change criterion

nodes.statement:
If $H^p(X_y,\mathcal F_y)=0$ for all $y$, then
$R^{p-1}f_*\mathcal F\otimes k(y)\simeq H^{p-1}(X_y,\mathcal F_y)$ for all $y$.
nodes.title: Vanishing in the preceding degree

nodes.statement:
If $R^kf_*\mathcal F=0$ for $k>k_0$, then $H^k(X_y,\mathcal F_y)=0$ for
$k>k_0$ and all $y$.
nodes.title: Higher vanishing

nodes.statement:
If $B$ is flat over $A$, then
\[
 H^p(X\times_Y\Spec B,\mathcal F\otimes_A B)\simeq H^p(X,\mathcal F)\otimes_A B.
\]
nodes.title: Flat base change

nodes.statement:
For complete $X$, any variety $T$, and a line bundle $L$ on $X\times T$, the
set of $t$ for which $L|_{X\times\{t\}}$ is trivial is closed. On this closed
set $T_1$, $L|_{X\times T_1}\simeq p_2^*M$ for a line bundle $M$ on $T_1$.
nodes.title: Seesaw theorem, provisional form

nodes.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be complete varieties, $Z$ any variety, with base points
$x_0,y_0,z_0$. If a line bundle $L$ on $X\times Y\times Z$ restricts
trivially to each of $\{x_0\}\times Y\times Z$,
$X\times\{y_0\}\times Z$, and $X\times Y\times\{z_0\}$, then $L$ is trivial.
nodes.title: Theorem of the cube

nodes.statement:
For a contravariant functor $T$ on complete varieties, define projections
$\pi_i$ and base-point inclusions $\sigma_i$ by omitting and restoring the
$i$th factor. Then
\[
 \alpha_T^n(\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_n)=\sum_{i=0}^n\pi_i^*(\xi_i),
 \qquad
 \beta_T^n(\eta)=(\sigma_0^*\eta,\sigma_2^*\eta,\ldots,\sigma_n^*\eta),
\]
and induction gives $T(\prod X_i)=\operatorname{Im}\alpha\oplus\ker\beta$.
The functor has order $n$ when $\alpha$ is surjective (equivalently $\beta$
injective). The cube theorem, when $Z$ is complete, says that $\Pic X$ is
quadratic.
nodes.title: Functorial order

nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be any variety and $x_0,x_1\in X$. Then there is an irreducible
curve $C$ on $X$ containing $x_0$ and $x_1$.
nodes.title: mumford-lem-cube-curve-joining

nodes.statement: $K(L)$ is a Zariski-closed subgroup of $X$.
nodes.title: Closedness of the translation kernel
Effective-divisor criterion

nodes.statement: Every abelian variety is projective.
nodes.title: Projectivity of abelian varieties

nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be complete of dimension $g$, $L$ invertible, and $\mathcal F$ coherent.
Write $P_{\mathcal F}(n)=\chi(\mathcal F\otimes L^n)$ and
$d_L(\mathcal F)/g!$ for its leading coefficient.  Then
\[
d_L(\mathcal F)=\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal F)\deg L.
\]
If $f:Y\to X$ is a surjective morphism of complete $g$-folds, then
\[
\deg f^*L=(\deg f)\deg L.
\]
nodes.title: Hilbert-polynomial degree

nodes.statement: For an abelian variety of dimension $g$, $\deg(n_X)=n^{2g}$.
nodes.title: Degree of multiplication

nodes.statement:
Let a finite group $G$ act on a variety $X$, with every orbit contained in an
affine open. Then there is a quotient variety $Y=X/G$ with
$\mathcal O_Y=\pi_*\mathcal O_X^G$; $\pi$ is finite, surjective, separable,
and etale when the action is free. If $X$ is affine, so is $Y$.
nodes.title: Finite group quotient

nodes.statement:
If $G$ acts freely on $X$ and $Y=X/G$, pullback is an equivalence between
coherent sheaves on $Y$ and coherent $G$-sheaves on $X$.  Its inverse is
$\mathcal G\mapsto\pi_*\mathcal G^G$, and locally free sheaves correspond with
the same rank.
nodes.title: Descent of coherent sheaves

nodes.statement:
For a finite subgroup $K$ of an abelian variety $X$, the quotient $X/K$ is an
abelian variety and $X\to X/K$ is an etale isogeny. Conversely, every isogeny
is a quotient by its finite kernel.
nodes.title: Translation quotients

nodes.statement:
If $G$ acts freely on $X$ and $Y=X/G$, then for characters $\alpha:G\to k^*$,
\[
 \widehat G\simeq\ker[\Pic Y\to\Pic X],
\]
and if $|G|$ is prime to the characteristic, every coherent sheaf on $Y$ is
a direct summand of $\pi_*(\pi^*\mathcal F)$.
nodes.title: Characters and descended line bundles

nodes.statement: An abelian variety $X$ is divisible and $X_n$ is finite for every $n>1$.
nodes.title: Divisibility and finite torsion

nodes.statement:
For $g=\dim X$,
\[
 \deg(n_X)=n^{2g},\qquad n_X\text{ is separable}\Longleftrightarrow p\nmid n.
\]
If $p\nmid n$, then $X_n\simeq(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g}$; for some
$0\le i\le g$, $X_{p^m}\simeq(\mathbf Z/p^m\mathbf Z)^i$.
nodes.title: Degree and separability of multiplication

nodes.statement:
$\Pic^0(X)$ is the subgroup of line bundles $L$ for which
$\phi_L(x)=T_x^*L\otimes L^{-1}$ is identically zero. In characteristic zero
it has a natural structure of an abelian variety, denoted $\widehat X$.
nodes.title: The dual variety

nodes.statement:
For every abelian variety $X$ over a characteristic-zero field there is an
abelian variety $\widehat X$ representing $\Pic^0(X)$, with a Poincare bundle
$P_X$ on $X\times\widehat X$ trivial on both coordinate axes. Every line
bundle in $\Pic^0(X)$ is represented uniquely by a point of $\widehat X$.
nodes.title: Dual abelian variety, characteristic zero

nodes.statement:
There is a canonical isomorphism $X\simeq\widehat{\widehat X}$.
If $f:X\to Y$ is an isogeny, then $\widehat f:\widehat Y\to\widehat X$ is an
isogeny and $\ker f$ and $\ker\widehat f$ are canonically dual finite groups.
nodes.title: Biduality

nodes.statement:
A divisorial correspondence between $X,Y$ is a line bundle on $X\times Y$
trivial on $\{0\}\times Y$ and $X\times\{0\}$.
nodes.title: Divisorial correspondence

nodes.statement:
For equal-dimensional $X,Y$ and a divisorial correspondence $Q$, the
conditions that $Q|_{\{x\}\times Y}$ be trivial only for $x=0$ and that
$Q|_{X\times\{y\}}$ be trivial only for $y=0$ are equivalent. When they hold,
$X\simeq\widehat Y$, $Y\simeq\widehat X$, and $Q$ is the Poincare bundle.
nodes.title: Characterization of the Poincare correspondence

nodes.statement:
For $L(H,\alpha)$ on $X=V/U$,
\[
 T_{\pi(a)}^*L(H,\alpha)\simeq L(H,\alpha\gamma_a),
 \qquad \gamma_a(u)=e^{2\pi iE(a,u)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 K(L)=U^\perp/U,
\quad U^\perp=\{a:E(a,u)\in\mathbf Z\ \forall u\in U\},
\]
and $L\in\Pic^0(X)$ iff $H=0$; $K(L)$ is finite iff $H$ is nondegenerate.
nodes.title: Analytic translation formula

nodes.statement:
For $X=V/U$, let
\[
 U'=\{l\in\overline T:\operatorname{Im}l(u)\in\mathbf Z\ \forall u\in U\}.
\]
Then $\widehat X=\overline T/U'$, and the Poincare bundle is
$L(H,\alpha)$ with
\[
 H((x_1,l_1),(x_2,l_2))=\overline{l_2(x_1)}+l_1(x_2),
 \qquad \alpha((u,l))=e^{-\pi i\operatorname{Im}l(u)}.
\]
The point represented by $l$ corresponds to $L(0,\alpha_l)$ with
$\alpha_l(u)=e^{2\pi i\operatorname{Im}l(u)}$.
nodes.title: Analytic construction of the dual

nodes.statement:
The two analytic descriptions of the map from $\overline T$ to
$\operatorname{Pic}^0(X)$ differ by the scalar normalization $2i$; explicitly,
the factor-of-automorphy description sends
\[
 l\longmapsto L(0,\alpha_l^*),
 \qquad \alpha_l^*(u)=e^{4\pi i\operatorname{Re}l(u)}.
\]
nodes.title: Normalization of the analytic dual identification

nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a compact connected complex Lie group.  Then $X$ is commutative.
nodes.title: Commutativity of a compact connected complex Lie group

nodes.statement:
The exponential map $\exp:V\to X$ is a surjective homomorphism of complex
Lie groups with kernel a lattice $U$ in $V$, and induces an isomorphism
$V/U\simeq X$.
nodes.title: Uniformization

nodes.statement:
As an abstract group, $X$ is divisible.  If $n\neq0$ and $X_n$ is the subgroup
of elements annihilated by $n$, then
\[
 X_n\simeq(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g}.
\]
nodes.title: Divisibility and torsion

nodes.statement:
There are canonical isomorphisms
\[
 H^r(X,\mathbf Z)\simeq
 \{\text{alternating $r$-forms }U\times\cdots\times U\to\mathbf Z\}.
\]
nodes.title: Integral cohomology

nodes.statement:
If $W$ is a complex vector space and $D\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\C}(W,\C)$,
then $D$ extends to $D\mathbin{\lrcorner}:\Lambda^pW\to\Lambda^{p-1}W$ by
\[
 D\mathbin{\lrcorner}(X_1\wedge\cdots\wedge X_p)=
 \sum_{k=1}^p(-1)^{p-k}D(X_k)X_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\widehat X_k\wedge\cdots\wedge X_p.
\]
If $DX_0=1$, then
$D\mathbin{\lrcorner}(\omega\wedge X_0)+(D\mathbin{\lrcorner}\omega)\wedge X_0=\omega$.
nodes.title: Interior multiplication

nodes.statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(V,\mathbf C)$ and
$\overline T=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C\text{-antilinear}}(V,\mathbf C)$.
Then
\[
 H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)\simeq\Lambda^q\overline T,
 \qquad
 H^q(X,\Omega^p)\simeq\Lambda^pT\otimes\Lambda^q\overline T.
\]
nodes.title: Dolbeault cohomology of a complex torus

nodes.statement:
For every $\omega\in\mathfrak a\otimes_{\mathbf C}A^\bullet$,
$\mu_A(\bar\partial\omega)=0$.
nodes.title: Integration kills invariant derivatives

nodes.statement:
For $\omega\in\mathfrak a\otimes_{\mathbf C}A^p$,
\[
 Q_\lambda(\bar\partial\omega)=(-1)^p2\pi i\,
 [Q_\lambda(\omega)\wedge\overline C(\lambda)].
\]
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients and $\bar\partial$

nodes.statement:
Under $H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)\simeq\Lambda^q\overline T$, cup product is
exterior product.  This follows by computing cup product in the differential
graded algebra resolving $\mathcal O_X$.
nodes.title: mumford-frag-cup-product

nodes.statement:
The map induced by cup product
\[
 \Lambda^qH^1(X,\mathcal O_X)\longrightarrow H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)
\]
is an isomorphism.
nodes.title: mumford-frag-cup-cor

nodes.statement:
The de Rham resolution gives
\[
 H^n(X,\C)\simeq
 \frac{\{d\text{-closed $n$-forms}\}}{d\{\text{$(n-1)$-forms}\}}.
\]
Every closed form differs by an exact form from a unique invariant form, so
\[
 H^n(X,\C)\simeq\Lambda^n\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf R}(V,\C).
\]
Since
\[
 \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf R}(V,\C)\simeq T\oplus\overline T,
\]
we obtain
\[
 H^n(X,\C)\simeq\Lambda^n(T\oplus\overline T)
 \simeq\bigoplus_{p+q=n}(\Lambda^pT\otimes\Lambda^q\overline T)
 \simeq\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^q(X,\Omega^p).
\]
This is the Hodge decomposition.
nodes.title: de Rham and Hodge decomposition

nodes.statement:
Under the evaluations
\[
 H^1(X,\mathbf Z)\simeq U^*,\qquad
 H^1(X,\C)\simeq T\oplus\overline T,\qquad
 H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)\simeq\overline T,
\]
the maps induced by $\mathbf Z\to\C\to\mathcal O_X$ are the inclusion
$U^*\subset T\oplus\overline T$ and projection onto $\overline T$.
nodes.title: Comparison of the three $H^1$ evaluations

nodes.statement: For every integer $p>0$, $H^p(\mathbf C^N,\mathcal O)=0$.
nodes.title: Vanishing on affine space

nodes.statement:
For every $p>0$, $H^p(\mathbf C^N,\mathcal O^*)=0$.  In particular, every
holomorphic line bundle on $\mathbf C^N$ is trivial.
nodes.title: Triviality on affine space

nodes.statement:
Writing $H^*=H^0(V,\mathcal O_V^*)$, the above construction gives an
isomorphism
\[
 H^1(U,H^*)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(X,\mathcal O_X^*).
\]
Explicitly, a $1$-cocycle $\{e_u\}$ defines the quotient of
$\mathbf C\times V$ by (A), and every line bundle arises in this way.
More generally there is a natural map
\[
 H^i(U,\Gamma(\mathcal F,\pi^*\mathcal F))\longrightarrow H^i(X,\mathcal F),
\]
When $H^i(V,\pi^*\mathcal F)=0$ for $i\ge1$, this natural map is an
isomorphism; in the present case this applies because
$H^i(V,\mathcal O_V^*)=0$ for $i\ge1$.
nodes.title: Factors of automorphy

nodes.statement:
The map $AF(u_1,u_2)=F(u_1,u_2)-F(u_2,u_1)$ induces an isomorphism
\[
 H^2(U,\mathbf Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda^2U,\mathbf Z)
 \simeq\Lambda^2\operatorname{Hom}(U,\mathbf Z),
\]
and $A(\xi\cup\eta)=\xi\wedge\eta$.
nodes.title: Alternation of group $2$-cocycles

nodes.statement:
The Chern class of the line bundle defined by $\{e_u\}$ is the alternating form
\[
 E(u_1,u_2)=f_{u_2}(z+u_1)+f_{u_1}(z)-f_{u_1+u_2}(z)-f_{u_2}(z),
\]
independent of $z$, where $e_u=e^{2\pi i f_u}$.
nodes.title: Chern class formula

nodes.statement:
After extending $E$ $\mathbf R$-linearly to $V$, one has
$E(ix,iy)=E(x,y)$.
nodes.title: Type $(1,1)$ condition

nodes.statement:
Hermitian forms $H$ on $V$ correspond bijectively to real skew-symmetric forms
$E$ satisfying $E(ix,iy)=E(x,y)$ by
\[
 E(x,y)=\operatorname{Im}H(x,y),\qquad H(x,y)=E(ix,y)+iE(x,y).
\]
nodes.title: Hermitian forms and invariant alternating forms

nodes.statement:
If $H$ is Hermitian, $E=\operatorname{Im}H$ is integral on $U$, then there is
$\alpha:U\to\mathbf C_1^*$ with
\[
 \alpha(u_1+u_2)=e^{i\pi E(u_1,u_2)}\alpha(u_1)\alpha(u_2),
\]
and
\[
 e_u(z)=\alpha(u)e^{\pi H(z,u)+\frac12\pi H(u,u)}
\]
is a $1$-cocycle whose Chern class is $E$.
nodes.title: Semicharacters

nodes.statement:
$L(H,\alpha)$ is the quotient of $\mathbf C\times V$ by
\[
 (\lambda,z)\longmapsto
 (\alpha(u)e^{\pi H(z,u)+\frac12\pi H(u,u)}\lambda,z+u).
\]
Moreover $L(H_1,\alpha_1)\otimes L(H_2,\alpha_2)\simeq
L(H_1+H_2,\alpha_1\alpha_2)$.
nodes.title: The bundle $L(H,\alpha)$

nodes.statement:
Every line bundle on $X=V/U$ is uniquely $L(H,\alpha)$ as above. There are
exact sequences
\[
0\to\operatorname{Hom}(U,\mathbf C^*)\to\{(H,\alpha)\}\to
\{H:(\operatorname{Im}H)(U\times U)\subset\mathbf Z\}\to0,
\]
and
\[
0\to\Pic^0X\to\Pic X\xrightarrow{c^1}
\ker[H^2(X,\mathbf Z)\to H^2(X,\mathcal O_X)]\to H^2(X,\mathcal O_X)\to0.
\]
nodes.title: Appell--Humbert

nodes.statement:
For $Y=X/G$ with $G$ free and discontinuous and $\pi:X\to Y$, every sheaf
$\mathcal F$ on $Y$ has a natural map
\[
 H^p(G,\Gamma(X,\pi^*\mathcal F))\to H^p(Y,\mathcal F).
\]
It is compatible with exact sequences and cup products, and is an isomorphism
if $H^i(X,\pi^*\mathcal F)=0$ for $i\ge1$.
nodes.title: Quotient-space cohomology map

nodes.statement:
Let $N=\{x:H(x,y)=0\ \forall y\}$.  If $H$ is degenerate, every
theta-function is constant on cosets of $N$, and a nonzero theta-function can
exist only if $\alpha|_{N\cap U}=1$; the associated sections factor through
$X/(N/(N\cap U))$, so $L(H,\alpha)$ is not ample.  If $H$ is negative on a
nonzero complex subspace, then it has no nonzero theta-functions.
nodes.title: Degenerate and negative Hermitian forms

nodes.statement:
If $H$ is positive definite and $E=\operatorname{Im}H$ is integral on $U$,
then
\[
 \dim H^0(X,L(H,\alpha))=\sqrt{\det_U E}.
\]
nodes.title: Dimension of theta-functions
Lefschetz

nodes.statement:
If $X$ is complete algebraic and $Y$ is a closed analytic subset of
$X_{\mathrm{hol}}$, then $Y$ is Zariski closed. A holomorphic map between
complete algebraic varieties is algebraic, and meromorphic functions on a
complete algebraic variety are rational.
nodes.title: Chow

nodes.statement:
For a complex torus $X=V/U$, the following are equivalent: $X$ is associated to
a projective algebraic variety; $X$ is associated to an algebraic variety;
$X$ has $g$ algebraically independent meromorphic functions; and there is a
positive definite Hermitian $H$ with $\operatorname{Im}H$ integral on $U$.
nodes.title: Algebraizability criterion

nodes.statement:
For almost all lattices $U$ in a $g$-dimensional complex vector space, the map
\[
 \Lambda^2_{\mathbf Z}U\longrightarrow\Lambda^2_{\mathbf C}V
\]
is injective. Hence almost all complex tori of dimension at least $2$ are
nonalgebraic.
nodes.title: Generic nonalgebraizability

nodes.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q$ and $X$ an abelian variety over
$K$. Then $X(K)$ is finitely generated.
nodes.title: Mordell--Weil

nodes.statement: For every $n>1$, $X(K)/nX(K)$ is finite.
nodes.title: Weak Mordell--Weil

nodes.statement:
There is a symmetric bilinear pairing $\langle\ ,\ \rangle:X(K)^2\to\mathbb R$
with $\langle x,x\rangle\ge0$ and with finitely many $x$ satisfying
$\langle x,x\rangle<C$ for every $C>0$.
nodes.title: Height pairing

nodes.statement:
If an abelian group $\Gamma$ has finite $\Gamma/n\Gamma$ for every $n>1$ and
has a pairing with the preceding two properties, then $\Gamma$ is finitely generated.
nodes.title: Formal finite-generation criterion

nodes.statement:
For $L=K(n_X^{-1}X(K))$, the composite of the fields obtained by adjoining
all $n$-division points of points of $X(K)$, $L/K$ is finite abelian.
nodes.title: Fundamental lemma

nodes.statement:
For $G={\rm Gal}(L/K)$,
\[
X(K)/nX(K)\hookrightarrow{\rm Hom}(G,X_n),\qquad
f_x(s)=s(n^{-1}x)-n^{-1}x.
\]
nodes.title: Kummer deduction

nodes.statement:
For a ring of integers $A$ of $K$, after shrinking $Y={\rm Spec}A_s$ there are
a projective $\widetilde X\to Y$, multiplication $\widetilde m$, and section
$\widetilde e$ whose generic fibre is $X$, whose closed fibres are abelian
varieties, and with $\widetilde X(Y)\simeq X(K)$.
nodes.title: Integral model

nodes.statement:
If $x\in\widetilde X(Y)$, then $n^{-1}(x)\to\operatorname{Spec}A_s$ is etale
where the residue characteristic does not divide $n$.
nodes.title: Etaleness of division points

nodes.statement:
There is a finite set $E$ of prime ideals of $A$ such that for $x\in X(K)$ and
$y\in n^{-1}(x)$, $K(y)/K$ is unramified outside $E$.
nodes.title: Unramified division fields

nodes.statement:
The maximal abelian exponent-$n$ extension of $K$ unramified outside fixed $E$
is finite.
nodes.title: Bounded Kummer extensions

nodes.statement:
\[
h(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=\frac1{[K:\mathbb Q]}\sum_vn_v\max_i\log|x_i|_v.\tag{6}
\]
This is well defined on $\mathbb P^n(K)$, invariant under scaling, nonnegative,
and independent of the field containing the coordinates.
nodes.title: Projective height

nodes.statement:
For $C,d>0$, finitely many $x\in\mathbb P^n(\overline K)$ satisfy
$h(x)\le C$ and $[K(x):K]\le d$.
nodes.title: Bounded height and degree

nodes.statement: Heights $h_1,h_2$ from two coordinate systems satisfy $h_1\sim h_2$.
nodes.title: Equivalent coordinate heights

nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be complete over $K$, and let $\varphi:X\to\mathbb P^k$ and
$\psi:X\to\mathbb P^l$ be $K$-morphisms. If
$\varphi^*\mathcal O(1)\simeq\psi^*\mathcal O(1)$, then
$h_\varphi\sim h_\psi$ on $X(\overline K)$.
nodes.title: Height of a line bundle embedding
Weil height theorem

nodes.statement:
If $h:\Gamma\to\mathbb R$ on an abelian group satisfies
\[
h(x_1+x_2+x_3)-\sum_{i<j}h(x_i+x_j)+\sum_i h(x_i)\sim0,\tag{8}
\]
then there are unique symmetric bilinear $b:\Gamma^2\to\mathbb R$ and
homomorphism $l:\Gamma\to\mathbb R$ such that
\[
h(x)\sim\widehat h(x)=\frac12b(x,x)+l(x).
\]
nodes.title: Approximate quadratic functions

nodes.statement:
For an abelian variety $X/K$ and $L\in{\rm Pic}X$, the Weil height $h_L$
satisfies (8). Hence $b_L,l_L$ and the Tate height $\widehat h_L$ are uniquely
defined.
nodes.title: Tate height

nodes.statement:
For $\varphi:X\to Y$ and $L\in{\rm Pic}Y$,
$\widehat h_{\varphi^*L}=\widehat h_L\circ\varphi$ and
$b_{\varphi^*L}=b_L\circ\varphi$, $l_{\varphi^*L}=l_L\circ\varphi$.
For $L^{-1}$, $b_{L^{-1}}=-b_L$ and $l_{L^{-1}}=-l_L$. If $L$ is symmetric,
$l_L=0$ and $\widehat h_L(x)=\frac12b_L(x,x)$.
nodes.title: Functoriality and symmetric bundles

nodes.statement:
A field of definition of an abelian variety $X/k$ is a subfield $k_0$ over
which a group scheme $X_0$ exists with $X_0\otimes_{k_0}k\simeq X$.
nodes.title: Field of definition

nodes.statement:
For abelian varieties $X,Y$ over algebraically closed $k$ and
$\ell\ne{\rm char}(k)$,
\[
\mathbb Z_\ell\otimes_{\mathbb Z}{\rm Hom}(X,Y)\xrightarrow{T_\ell}
{\rm Hom}_{\mathbb Z_\ell}(T_\ell(X),T_\ell(Y)) \tag{1}
\]
is injective. Choose a common field of definition $k_0$, of finite type over
the prime field, and let $\bar k_0$ be its algebraic closure in $k$. Then
$G={\rm Gal}(\bar k_0/k_0)$ acts continuously on $T_\ell(X),T_\ell(Y)$.
Every homomorphism $X\to Y$ is defined over a finite extension $k_1/k_0$ in
$\bar k_0$; if $H={\rm Gal}(\bar k_0/k_1)$, then
\[
 h\varphi(x)=\varphi(hx)
\]
for every $h\in H$ and every $\bar k_0$-point $x$ of $X$.
nodes.title: Tate-module invariants and field of definition

nodes.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be abelian varieties defined over a finite field $k_0$. Then
the homomorphism
\[
 \mathbb Z_l\otimes_{\mathbb Z}{\rm Hom}(X,Y)\longrightarrow
 {\rm Hom}_{\mathbb Z_l}(T_l(X),T_l(Y))^{(G)}
\]
is an isomorphism, where $G={\rm Gal}(k/k_0)$ and the superscript denotes
elements fixed by some neighborhood of the identity.
nodes.title: Tate

nodes.statement:
It suffices to show that
\[
 \mathbb Q_l\otimes_{\mathbb Z_l}{\rm Hom}(X,Y)
 =\mathbb Q_l\otimes_{\mathbb Q}{\rm Hom}^{0}(X,Y)
 \longrightarrow {\rm Hom}_{\mathbb Q_l}(V_l(X),V_l(Y))^{(G)} \tag{3}
\]
is bijective, where $V_l(X)=\mathbb Q_l\otimes_{\mathbb Z_l}T_l(X)$.
nodes.title: Step I

nodes.statement:
It suffices to show, for every abelian variety $X$ over a finite field, that
\[
 \mathbb Q_l\otimes_{\mathbb Q}{\rm End}^{0}(X)
 \xrightarrow{\lambda}{\rm End}_{\mathbb Q_l}(V_l(X))^{(G)} \tag{4}
\]
is an isomorphism.
nodes.title: Step II

nodes.statement:
It suffices to show that $\lambda$ is an isomorphism for one $l$ and that
\[\dim_{\mathbb Q_l}{\rm End}(V_l(X))^{(G)}\]
is independent of $l\ne {\rm char}\,k$.
nodes.title: Step III

nodes.statement:
Let $E$ be the image of $\lambda$, and let $F$ be the intersection over all
neighborhoods of $e$ in $G$ of the subalgebras generated in
${\rm End}_{\mathbb Q_l}(V_l)$ by these neighborhoods. To establish (4), it
suffices to show that $F$ is the commutant of $E$ in ${\rm End}(V_l)$.
nodes.title: Step IV

nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be an abelian variety over $k_0$ and $l$ a prime. For every integer
$d\geq1$, there are, up to isomorphism, only finitely many abelian varieties
$Y$ over $k_0$ such that (a) $Y$ has an ample line bundle $L$ defined over
$k_0$ with $\chi(L)=d$, and (b) there is a $k_0$-isogeny $Y\to X$ of $l$-power
degree.
nodes.title: Hypothesis $(k_0,X,l)$

nodes.statement:
If $k_0$ is finite, $d>0$, and $g>0$, only finitely many isomorphism classes
of $g$-dimensional abelian varieties $Y$ over $k_0$ carry an ample line bundle
$L$ defined over $k_0$ with $\chi(L)=d$.
nodes.title: Finite-field finiteness

nodes.statement:
Let $X$ be quasi-projective over $k_0$ and $\Pi$ a finite group of
automorphisms such that (i) the automorphisms of $\Pi$ are defined over a
separably algebraic extension of $k_0$, and (ii) $\Pi^\sigma=\Pi$ for every
automorphism $\sigma$ of $\bar k_0$ over $k_0$. Then $X/\Pi$ and
$X\to X/\Pi$ are defined over $k_0$.
nodes.title: Quotient descent

nodes.statement:
If $L\in{\rm Pic}^0Y$ is defined over $\bar k_0$ and $\sigma\in
{\rm Gal}(\bar k_0/k_0)$, then $\sigma(L)\in{\rm Pic}^0Y$.
nodes.title: Galois stability of ${\rm Pic}^0$

nodes.statement:
Let $Y$ be complete over $k_0$ with a $k_0$-point, let $k_1/k_0$ be Galois,
and let $L$ on $\overline Y$ be defined over $k_1$ with
$\sigma(L)\simeq L$ for every $\sigma\in{\rm Gal}(k_1/k_0)$. Then $L$ is
defined over $k_0$.
nodes.title: Descent of invariant line bundles

nodes.statement:
Suppose $X$ and an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$ are defined over $k_0$,
$l\ne {\rm char}\,k_0$, and Hypothesis $(k_0,X,l)$ holds. If
$W\subset V_l(X)$ is $G$-stable and maximal isotropic for $E^L$, then there
is an element $u\in F$ with $u(V_l(X))=W$.
nodes.title: Step V

nodes.statement:
Suppose Hypothesis $(k_1,X,l)$ holds for every finite algebraic extension
$k_1/k_0$, and $F$ is a product of copies of $\mathbb Q_l$. Then (4) is an
isomorphism.
nodes.title: Step VI

nodes.statement:
After a finite extension assume every element of ${\rm End}\,X$ is defined.
For Frobenius $\pi$, the algebra $\mathbb Q[\pi]$ is commutative semisimple.
There are infinitely many primes $l$ for which
$\mathbb Q_l\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb Q[\pi]$ is a product of copies of
$\mathbb Q_l$.
nodes.title: Step VII: end of proof

nodes.statement:
For every non-constant $F(X)\in\mathbb Z[X]$, there are infinitely many primes
$l$ for which $F(X)\equiv0\pmod l$ has a solution in $\mathbb Z$.
nodes.title: Infinitely many prime roots

nodes.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be absolutely semisimple endomorphisms of finite-dimensional
$k$-vector spaces $V,W$, with
\[
 P_A=\prod_p p^{m(p)},\qquad P_B=\prod_p p^{n(p)}
\]
the decompositions into powers of distinct irreducible monic polynomials. Then
\[
 E=\{\varphi\in{\rm Hom}_k(V,W):\varphi A=B\varphi\}
\]
has dimension
\[
 r(P_A,P_B)=\sum_p m(p)n(p)\deg p,
\]
and this integer is unchanged by extension of $k$.
nodes.title: Commutants of semisimple endomorphisms

nodes.statement:
For abelian varieties $X,Y$ over a finite field $k_0$,
\[
 \mathbb Z_l\otimes_{\mathbb Z}{\rm Hom}_{k_0}(X,Y)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}{\rm Hom}_{\mathbb Z_l}(T_l(X),T_l(Y))^G.
\]
nodes.title: Tate, strengthened form

nodes.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be abelian varieties over a finite field $k_0$, with Frobenius
characteristic polynomials $P_X,P_Y$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\operatorname{rank}{\rm Hom}_{k_0}(X,Y)=r(P_X,P_Y)$.
\item The following are equivalent: (b1) $Y$ is $k_0$-isogenous to an abelian
subvariety of $X$ defined over $k_0$; (b2) $V_l(Y)$ is $G$-isomorphic to a
$G$-subspace of $V_l(X)$ for some $l$; (b3) $P_Y$ divides $P_X$.
\item The following are equivalent: (c1) $X,Y$ are $k_0$-isogenous; (c2)
$P_X=P_Y$; (c3) they have the same number of $k_1$-rational points for every
finite extension $k_1/k_0$.
\end{enumerate}
nodes.title: Tate's applications

nodes.statement:
If $Y$ is an abelian subvariety of an abelian variety $X$ over a finite field
$k_0$ and is $k_0$-closed, then $Y$ is an abelian variety defined over $k_0$.
Moreover, there is a $k_0$-defined abelian subvariety $Z$ with $Y+Z=X$ and
$Y\cap Z$ finite. Consequently every $k_0$-abelian variety is isogenous to a
product of $k_0$-simple abelian varieties, and if
$X\sim\prod_iX_i^{n_i}$ with pairwise non-isogenous simple $X_i$, then
\[
 {\rm End}_{k_0}^{0}X\simeq\prod_iM_{n_i}(D_i),
 \qquad D_i={\rm End}_{k_0}^{0}(X_i).
\]
nodes.title: Descent of closed abelian subvarieties

nodes.statement:
Let $X$ have dimension $g$ over a finite field $k_0$, with Frobenius $\pi$ and
characteristic polynomial $P$. Put $F=\mathbb Q[\pi]$ and
$E={\rm End}_{k_0}^{0}(X)$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is the center of the semisimple algebra $E$.
\item $E$ contains a semisimple maximal commutative $\mathbb Q$-subalgebra
of rank $2g$.
\item The following are equivalent: $[E:\mathbb Q]=2g$; $P$ has no multiple
root; $E=F$; $E$ is commutative.
\item The following are equivalent: $[E:\mathbb Q]=(2g)^2$; $P$ is a power
of a linear polynomial; $F=\mathbb Q$; $E=M_g(D_p)$ for the quaternion division
algebra $D_p$ split away from $p,\infty$; $X$ is isogenous to the $g$th power
of a supersingular curve with all endomorphisms defined over $k_0$.
\item $X$ is isogenous to a power of a $k_0$-simple variety iff $P$ is a power
of a $\mathbb Q$-irreducible polynomial. In that case $E$ is central simple over
$F$, split at finite primes not dividing $p$ and nonsplit at real primes.
\end{enumerate}
nodes.title: Structure of endomorphism algebras

nodes.statement:
Any two elliptic curves over finite fields with isomorphic algebras of complex
multiplications are isogenous over the algebraic closure. In particular, any
two supersingular elliptic curves are isogenous.
nodes.title: Elliptic curves
